title: Hourly to Annual: Your NRL Salary Conversion Guide
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary using a 38-hour week, 52-week year. Includes tax, super, fortnight pay, and comparison to NRL salary figures.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week and 52-week year, your annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by your weekly hours (usually 38 for full-time) then by 52 weeks. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 gross per year. Use [the timesheet](/) to do this instantly.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For award-free employees, the national minimum wage casual rate is $33.05 per hour from 1 July 2026. See [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) for more.

faqs.q: How is tax calculated on my annual salary?
faqs.a: Use the 2026–27 resident tax rates: tax-free up to $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. Add the 2% Medicare levy. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool estimates your net pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to an Annual Salary

Whether you're comparing your earnings to an NRL salary or planning your household budget, understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay is essential. This guide walks you through the standard conversion using a 38-hour week and a 52-week year, explains the difference between the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and shows how super and tax are calculated.

### The 38-Hour Week and 52-Week Year

Most full-time roles in Australia are based on a 38-hour week. To get your annual gross pay, multiply your hourly rate by 38, then by 52. For example, $26.44 per hour (the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026) gives $1004.90 per week and $52,254.80 per year. If you're on an award, check your specific classification in the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. Simply multiply your weekly gross by 2. Using the minimum wage example, that's $2009.80 per fortnight. This is a handy figure for budgeting and comparing to typical NRL salary contracts, which are often quoted annually but paid fortnightly.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours. This applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. However, most workers are covered by an industry or occupation award, which often has higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) with exact rates for each classification.

### Casual Loading

If you're a casual employee, you're entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For the National Minimum Wage, that's $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. When using [the timesheet](/) to convert your hourly rate, check the 'casual loading' box if you're casual. Never enter a rate that already includes the loading; the tool adds it for you.

## Superannuation Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. It does not come out of your hourly rate. For 2026–27, the maximum contribution base is $270,830. So if your annual salary exceeds that, super is capped. For example, on $100,000 gross, your employer adds $12,000 in super. This is separate from your take-home pay. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and Medicare

Your annual gross salary is used to calculate income tax. The 2026–27 resident tax rates are:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,370 plus 45% on excess over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low incomes). Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool applies these rates to estimate your net pay after tax and Medicare.

## Using the Timesheet

[The timesheet](/) is the simplest way to convert your hourly rate. Enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading), select your hours per week (default 38), and the tool shows annual, fortnightly, and weekly gross. Check the casual loading box if applicable. The results also estimate tax and super. Remember, this is an estimate – it assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice.

## Comparing to NRL Salary

NRL salary figures are often reported as annual amounts. While the average NRL player earns well above the national average, the conversion method is identical. If you know an NRL player's hourly rate (unlikely to be public), multiply by 38 and 52. More practically, you can use this guide to see how your own pay stacks up against that benchmark. The key is understanding the components: base rate, loading, super, and tax.

## Final Notes

Always check your award or agreement for exact rates. The Fair Work Commission and Fair Work Ombudsman are the authoritative sources. Use [reference tables](/data) for historical rates and [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) for the latest. This guide helps you make sense of your pay, whether you're a minimum wage worker or aiming for an NRL salary.
